scenes.visual: Title card: Two Jobs, One Division.

scenes.tts: A stem cell has two jobs. It must stay a stem cell, and it must make cells that differentiate. How can one division do both?
scenes.visual: A round stem cell with two labels beside it: stay a stem cell; make cells that differentiate. The question appears as on-screen text.
scenes.narration: A stem cell has two jobs. It must stay a stem cell, and it must make cells that differentiate. How can one division do both?

scenes.tts: In a symmetric division, the daughters are alike.
scenes.visual: The stem cell splits into two identical daughters. Label: symmetric.
scenes.narration: In a symmetric division, the daughters are alike.

scenes.tts: Two progenitors enlarge the pool. Two differentiating cells spend it.
scenes.visual: Two panels: two progenitors (pool counter goes up) and two differentiating cells (pool counter goes down).
scenes.narration: Two progenitors enlarge the pool. Two differentiating cells spend it.

scenes.tts: In an asymmetric division, the daughters take different fates. Often one stays a progenitor, and the other moves toward a fate.
scenes.visual: Third panel: one daughter stays a progenitor, the other changes colour and moves away. Pool counter stays the same. Label: asymmetric.
scenes.narration: In an asymmetric division, the daughters take different fates. Often one stays a progenitor, and the other moves toward a fate.

scenes.tts: Asymmetry can be built from inside. The mother gathers a protein on one side of its cortex.
scenes.visual: Inside panel: a mother cell with a gold crescent under the membrane on one side. Label: cortex, the layer just under the membrane.
scenes.narration: Asymmetry can be built from inside. The mother gathers a protein on one side of its cortex.

scenes.tts: That protein is called a determinant. The mother lines its spindle up, so only one daughter inherits it.
scenes.visual: The spindle rotates to point at the crescent; the furrow cuts so the gold crescent ends up in one daughter. Label: determinant.
scenes.narration: That protein is called a determinant. The mother lines its spindle up, so only one daughter inherits it.

scenes.tts: Or it can come from outside. Only one daughter stays touching a niche, cells that signal it to remain a stem cell.
scenes.visual: Outside panel: two alike daughters beside a row of niche cells; one stays in contact and keeps its colour, the other is pushed away and differentiates.
scenes.narration: Or it can come from outside. Only one daughter stays touching a niche, cells that signal it to remain a stem cell.

scenes.tts: Our first map is a fly bristle, a small sense organ of four cells.
scenes.visual: Map 1 title. A schematic bristle on a patch of fly skin: a hair shaft rising from a socket.
scenes.narration: Our first map is a fly bristle, a small sense organ of four cells.

scenes.tts: A neuron, a sheath cell that wraps it, and two outer cells that build the hair and socket.
scenes.visual: The four cells are drawn and labelled one by one: neuron, sheath cell, hair cell, socket cell.
scenes.narration: A neuron, a sheath cell that wraps it, and two outer cells that build the hair and socket.

scenes.tts: In the classic scheme, all four come from one sensory organ precursor, in three divisions.
scenes.caption: In the classic scheme, all four come from one sensory organ precursor (SOP), in three divisions.
scenes.visual: A lineage tree grows downward from one cell labelled sensory organ precursor (SOP). Small corner label: classic simplified map; the adult lineage also makes a glial cell.
scenes.narration: In the classic scheme, all four come from one sensory organ precursor (SOP), in three divisions.

scenes.tts: The precursor makes an outer precursor and an inner precursor. The outer one makes the hair cell and the socket cell.
scenes.visual: The tree fills in: SOP to outer precursor (pIIa) and inner precursor (pIIb); outer precursor to hair cell and socket cell.
scenes.narration: The precursor makes an outer precursor and an inner precursor. The outer one makes the hair cell and the socket cell.

scenes.tts: The inner one makes the neuron and the sheath cell.
scenes.visual: Inner precursor to neuron and sheath cell. The full four-cell tree is shown.
scenes.narration: The inner one makes the neuron and the sheath cell.

scenes.tts: At each division, one sister hears a signal called Notch, and the other does not. Which is which?
scenes.visual: At each of the three divisions, one daughter gets a blank label: hears Notch? The labels stay blank. Colour key: Notch-on teal, Notch-off grey, not yet filled in.
scenes.narration: At each division, one sister hears a signal called Notch, and the other does not. Which is which?

scenes.tts: Our second map is a neuroblast, a stem cell of the fly's central nervous system.
scenes.visual: Map 2 title. A neuroblast leaving a sheet of epithelial cells.
scenes.narration: Our second map is a neuroblast, a stem cell of the fly's central nervous system.

scenes.tts: In most neuroblasts, each division is unequal. The large top daughter stays a neuroblast.
scenes.visual: The neuroblast divides into a large apical daughter, labelled neuroblast, and a small basal daughter. Labels: apical (top), basal (bottom).
scenes.narration: In most neuroblasts, each division is unequal. The large top daughter stays a neuroblast.

scenes.tts: The small bottom daughter is a ganglion mother cell. It divides once more, into two neurons or glia.
scenes.visual: The small daughter is labelled ganglion mother cell (GMC); it divides into two cells labelled neuron or glia.
scenes.narration: The small bottom daughter is a ganglion mother cell. It divides once more, into two neurons or glia.

scenes.tts: Division after division, the neuroblast stays one neuroblast. Each division adds one ganglion mother cell, which divides once.
scenes.visual: Repeated divisions. A counter reads neuroblasts: 1, 1, 1, 1. Each new GMC divides once into two neuron-or-glia daughters; a second counter labelled cumulative GMCs produced ticks up.
scenes.narration: Division after division, the neuroblast stays one neuroblast. Each division adds one ganglion mother cell, which divides once.

scenes.tts: These maps raise four puzzles. How can two sisters born side by side differ?
scenes.visual: Both maps side by side. Puzzle 1 appears as on-screen text.
scenes.narration: These maps raise four puzzles. How can two sisters born side by side differ?

scenes.tts: What does the inherited protein do? How does the mother put it on one side? And what happens when the sorting fails?
scenes.visual: Puzzles 2, 3 and 4 appear in turn under puzzle 1.
scenes.narration: What does the inherited protein do? How does the mother put it on one side? And what happens when the sorting fails?

scenes.tts: Here is the idea to carry. The mother puts a protein called Numb on one side, and aims its spindle at it.
scenes.visual: Rule card, first half. A mother cell with a gold Numb crescent; the spindle swings to point at it.
scenes.narration: Here is the idea to carry. The mother puts a protein called Numb on one side, and aims its spindle at it.

scenes.tts: The daughter that inherits Numb cannot hear Notch. So it takes the Notch-off fate of that division. This holds where a Notch signal is on offer.
scenes.visual: Rule card, second half. The gold daughter turns grey (Notch-off); its sister turns teal (hears Notch). Small label: when a Notch signal is on offer.
scenes.narration: The daughter that inherits Numb cannot hear Notch. So it takes the Notch-off fate of that division. This holds where a Notch signal is on offer.

scenes.tts: One division can do both jobs, if the mother marks a side and only one daughter inherits it.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: mark a side, aim the spindle, one daughter inherits.
scenes.narration: One division can do both jobs, if the mother marks a side and only one daughter inherits it.

scenes.visual: Hold on the takeaway card.
